messages.author: fce42188ed75fb56
messages.subject: Saving/loading shiny session state?
parts:
Hi all,

we've been using shiny internally for (to use big words) "exploratory data analysis" in a project for some time and it's absolutely fabulous. However, working with a shiny application shows that there is a number of capabilities that "would be very nice to have". I understand that proper authentication (and maybe user management/authorization) will be introduced later - at least in the "enterprise edition". What I would be after now is saving and reloading session state. 

Two use cases as example:
- The user works on the data (effectively clicks around for some time, changing inputs) and finds just the visualization he wants. He closes the browser; next time when he opens it, he would like to see this state.
- The user wants to be able to record visualization states (for various "findings") and recall them one-by-one for a live, step-by-step demonstration.

At some level, both cases boil down to the ability to save and load (full or partial) session states. I think that to some extent this can be done manually in the code (I haven't really had the time to think through and implement the tricks that seem to be applicable); my question is whether there is "platform support" or is it in the scope of future development at all.

Best regards
Imre

messages.author: f04a46ca36d79541
messages.subject: Re: Saving/loading shiny session state?
parts: Waiting eagerly also :)

On Tuesday, March 5, 2013 at 5:39:59 AM UTC-5, Imre Kocsis wrote:
Hi all,

we've been using shiny internally for (to use big words) "exploratory data analysis" in a project for some time and it's absolutely fabulous. However, working with a shiny application shows that there is a number of capabilities that "would be very nice to have". I understand that proper authentication (and maybe user management/authorization) will be introduced later - at least in the "enterprise edition". What I would be after now is saving and reloading session state. 

Two use cases as example:
- The user works on the data (effectively clicks around for some time, changing inputs) and finds just the visualization he wants. He closes the browser; next time when he opens it, he would like to see this state.
- The user wants to be able to record visualization states (for various "findings") and recall them one-by-one for a live, step-by-step demonstration.

At some level, both cases boil down to the ability to save and load (full or partial) session states. I think that to some extent this can be done manually in the code (I haven't really had the time to think through and implement the tricks that seem to be applicable); my question is whether there is "platform support" or is it in the scope of future development at all.

Best regards
Imre
